name: LLM Text Generation & Analysis
summary: Versatile multi-provider LLM node supporting text generation, image analysis, prompt engineering, and content transformation. Supports Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, Claude, GPT-4, and other providers with vision capabilities, generating coherent text outputs with fine-grained control over temperature, token limits, and system prompts in 1-10 seconds.

inputs.description: Text input for the LLM. Can be a direct prompt, instruction template, question, content to transform, or system/user message combination. Supports Markdown and structured text for complex reasoning tasks.

Optional image(s) for vision-based analysis. Enables image description, style extraction, object detection, scene understanding, and visual question answering when provided to models with vision capabilities.

outputs.description: Generated text output from the LLM. Can be creative writing, analysis, structured data (JSON/CSV), code snippets, or transformed content depending on input prompt.
Generation metadata including model used, tokens generated, tokens consumed (for prompt), temperature applied, stop reason, provider, and cost estimation for billing and performance tracking.

executionNotes: This node provides a unified abstraction over multiple LLM providers (Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, Claude, GPT-4, Llama 2/3, and others). The provider and model fields control routing at execution time. Advanced parameters include temperature (0-2, controlling randomness), maxTokens (output length limit), top_p (diversity control), frequency_penalty, and presence_penalty. Vision-enabled models (Gemini, Claude, GPT-4) accept optional images for analysis. Supports system prompts for behavior control, few-shot examples for in-context learning, and structured output modes (JSON, YAML) when supported. Used extensively in the pipeline for prompt enhancement (expanding vague text into detailed image/video prompts), image analysis (extracting style attributes, object lists, composition notes), and content classification (determining media type, theme, mood). Typical latency: 1-10 seconds depending on model and output length.

exampleConnections.scenario: Prompt enhancement: Transform a simple user query ('a cool robot') into a detailed, stylized image prompt suitable for nanoBanana generation.
Image analysis and description: Analyze generated images to extract style descriptors, composition details, and mood for quality assurance or iterative refinement.
Iterative image generation: Use LLM to refine image prompts based on generation history and user feedback, enabling goal-directed creative optimization.
Video prompt engineering: Expand still image descriptions into narrative prompts with camera directions and motion cues for video generation.
Audio description generation: Create music or narration descriptions from image/video context, bridging visual and audio modalities.
Content transformation: Rewrite, summarize, translate, or stylistically transform text (e.g., marketing copy → technical documentation, English → emoji descriptions).
Multi-step reasoning: Chain multiple LLM calls for complex reasoning, each refining output of the previous for hierarchical problem-solving and validation.
